envelope.author: planner
envelope.reason: Decompose the amended `skill routing` concept (29799b5f) into its one unit of work: the projector gives every agent its skills' closure over composition, on every harness at the rung it can carry.
envelope.cause: design amendment 29799b5f to `skill routing`: every agent is given its role's skills together with everything they compose

spec.name: agent-skill-closure
spec.intent: Every projected agent is given the closure of its skills over `composition`: its skills as `holds` resolved them (the role's first, then the holder's declared), followed by every skill they transitively compose, breadth-first in each cell's declaration order, each name once. The closure resolves each composed name against the projection's resolved skill roster (`resolveSkills`), so a later plugin's same-name cell override changes it, a name absent from the roster is kept and not expanded, and a composition cycle terminates. It is computed once, in `projectPluginSet`, from that roster and before any `agentDef`, by a function beside `resolveSkills`; adapters render the list they are handed and compute nothing. `HarnessAdapter` gains one required member declaring whether an agent definition can name skills the harness preloads. omp says yes and emits `autoloadSkills` as today (its launcher already renders that key as required reading for a main session). claude says yes and emits a `skills` front-matter sequence, the field Claude Code's subagent schema preloads (https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents). codex says no, because its agent TOML has no such field (only `skills.config` enable/disable), so projection degrades it per the fidelity ladder, whose floor is a steer and never silence: no native field is emitted, the closure reaches the agent as a declaration (a required-reading section at the end of `developer_instructions` naming each skill in closure order), and one warning per skill-bearing agent names the agent, the harness and the skills. The claims that claude has no equivalent (the schema `Agent.skills` doc comment, the `agentToOmpMd` comments) and the canon test comment calling the omp list verbatim are corrected; forge's README documents the closure and each harness's rung; a changeset records it for `@cratylus/forge` (minor) and `@cratylus/schema` (patch).
accept: After `pnpm project`, `grep -h '^autoloadSkills:' .cratylus/omp/agents/{architect,mav,kino,nico}.md` prints exactly four lines, each `autoloadSkills: ["design", "deliver", "plan", "note"]` (at 29799b5f each prints `["design", "deliver"]`).

After `pnpm project`, the front matter of `.cratylus/claude/agents/<agent>.md`, parsed as YAML, has `skills` equal to [design, deliver, plan, note] for architect, mav, kino and nico, [plan, design, note] for planner, [design] for assayer, and no `skills` key for implementer.

After `pnpm project`, the `developer_instructions` of `.cratylus/codex/agents/<agent>.toml` ends with a required-reading section naming design, deliver, plan, note in that order for architect, mav, kino and nico, plan, design, note for planner, and design for assayer; implementer's carries no such section, and no codex agent TOML has a `skills` key.

`pnpm exec cratylus project --harness codex --out "$(mktemp -d)"` writes to stderr exactly one skill warning for each skill-bearing agent (architect, assayer, kino, mav, nico, planner: six, counted at 29799b5f), each naming the agent, `codex` and that agent's skills, and none naming implementer; the same command with `--harness claude` and with `--harness omp` writes no skill warning.

`pnpm --filter @cratylus/forge exec vitest run test/project/skill-closure.test.ts` passes, and fails if `projectPluginSet` hands adapters the declared list unexpanded: projecting its own fixture plugin it pins a transitive chain (a composes b, b composes c) emitted declared-first then breadth-first, a name reached twice emitted once, a composition cycle terminating, a later plugin's same-name skill cell changing the closure, the claude `skills` and omp `autoloadSkills` fields, and the codex warning plus required-reading declaration.
`grep -rnE 'claude and codex have no|neither claude nor codex' packages/*/src` prints nothing.
